title: Four pre-interview prep moves for architects
oneliner: Research the company's journey, match your experience to the job description, rehearse with a mock interview, and walk in with one project you know cold.
says: He gives four steps: study the company profile to understand where they are in their modernization or cloud migration journey and what their strategy is; read the job description thoroughly and match it against your experience until the fit is tight; run a mock interview with a close friend and fix whatever the feedback surfaces; and pick one key or innovative project from your past work that you can explain in complete depth.
explained: Each step targets a different failure mode. Company research stops generic answers - when you can say 'you are mid-migration from X to Y, and here is where I have done exactly that,' you stop sounding like every other candidate. Job-description matching stops you from preparing for the job you wish it were instead of the job it is.

The mock interview exists because speaking answers out loud is a different skill from knowing them; the first time you say an answer should not be in front of the panel. And the one deep project is your proof of depth: interviewers probe one story hard to test whether your resume is real. A project you know cold - decisions, trade-offs, what broke, what you would do differently - carries the whole interview.
takeaway: Preparation is specific, not general: their strategy, this job description, spoken rehearsal, one project in full depth.
